description: Opens the Layouts panel listing every layout page in the file for quick navigation, renaming and management. Much faster than tab-hunting in documents with many sheets.

name: Leader
description: Draws an arrowed leader line with attached text. The standard tool for calling up notes against specific parts of a drawing.

name: Length
description: Reports the true length of curves and edges. Used for quantities such as handrail runs, skirting lengths and cable routes.

name: Libraries
description: Opens the Libraries panel for browsing content such as materials, environments and textures, ready to drag into the model. A shop window for render assets.

name: Lights
description: Opens the Lights panel listing all lights in the model, where you can select, toggle and edit them. The control room for a rendering's lighting setup.

name: Line
description: Draws a single straight line between two picked points. The most basic drafting tool, used constantly for construction lines, edges and setting-out geometry.

name: Lines
description: Draws a connected chain of line segments where each segment becomes a separate line object, unlike Polyline which makes one joined object. Useful when you want individually editable segments.

name: LineThroughPt
description: Fits a single best-fit line through a set of selected points. A quick regression helper for finding the underlying direction in survey points or scan data.

name: LinetypeDisplay
description: Controls how linetypes such as dashed and dotted patterns display in model viewports, including their scaling. Lets you check that centre lines and hidden lines will read correctly before printing.

name: Linetypes
description: Opens the document's linetype list, where you load and manage dash patterns used by curves and layers. Set these up early so drawings export and print with correct line conventions.

name: List
description: Dumps the full internal data structure of an object, down to knots and control points. A deep debugging tool for advanced users and developers.

name: LoadScript
description: Loads a RhinoScript file into the session so its subroutines are available to run. Part of the classic RhinoScript automation workflow.

name: Lock
description: Makes selected objects visible but unselectable, greyed in the viewport. Perfect for reference geometry and context you must see but never nudge.

name: LockSwap
description: Swaps the locked state of everything: locked objects unlock and unlocked objects lock. Quick for alternating between editing a set of objects and protecting it.

name: LockViewport
description: Locks the active detail so its view cannot be accidentally panned or zoomed. Essential once a layout detail is set to a precise drawing scale.

name: Loft
description: Fits a surface through an ordered series of profile curves, with style options from tight to loose. A staple for canopies, hulls and any form defined by cross-sections.

name: Login
description: Signs in to your Rhino account for licensing and cloud services. Needed when using Cloud Zoo licences or shared team resources.

name: Logout
description: Signs out of your Rhino account, releasing the licence and cloud services on this machine. Use it before switching accounts or freeing a licence for a colleague.

name: MacroEditor
description: Opens an editor for writing and testing command macros, with a button to run them directly. The stepping stone between typed commands and full scripting.

name: Macros
description: Opens the Macros panel where command macros can be stored, organised and run without writing full scripts. A convenient home for the repetitive command sequences you use every day.

name: Maelstrom
description: Spirals objects around an axis so they whirl progressively with radius. A specialist deformer for vortex-like patterns and twisted radial compositions.

name: Make2D
description: Generates flat 2D line drawings of the model from a view, with hidden lines on separate layers. The bridge from 3D model to plans, sections and elevations for drafting.

name: MakeHole
description: Cuts a hole through a solid using a closed profile curve you supply. The general-purpose opening cutter for shaped penetrations and window reveals.

name: MakeNonPeriodic
description: Converts a closed periodic curve or surface into a non-periodic one, introducing a seam that can hold a kink. Sometimes needed before edits that require a defined start and end.

name: MakePeriodic
description: Converts a closed curve or surface so it has no kink at its seam, making it smoothly continuous all the way round. Useful before building smooth closed lofts or revolves.

name: MakeSubDFriendly
description: Rebuilds a curve so its structure suits SubD tools, avoiding surprises when creating SubD geometry from curves. Run it on profile curves before lofting or sweeping into SubD.

name: MakeUniform
description: Makes the knot spacing of a curve or surface uniform, evening out how control points influence the shape. The geometry may shift slightly, so use it on design surfaces rather than fitted data.

name: MakeUniformUV
description: Makes a surface's knot spacing uniform in the U or V direction you choose, rather than both at once. Gives more control than MakeUniform when only one direction is misbehaving.

name: MappingWidget
description: Shows the texture-mapping widget for the selected objects so you can move, rotate and scale how textures wrap onto them. Reach for it when a material's pattern sits at the wrong size or angle.

name: MappingWidgetOff
description: Hides the texture-mapping widgets shown by MappingWidget. Tidies the viewport once mapping adjustments are done.

name: MarkFoci
description: Places point objects at the foci of selected ellipses and conic curves. Useful for setting-out geometry that depends on focal points, such as reflector or whispering-gallery studies.

name: Match
description: Adjusts the end of one curve to meet another with position, tangency or curvature continuity. Essential prep before lofting or sweeping surfaces that must flow together.

name: MatchAnnotation
description: Applies the properties of one annotation to other annotations so notes and dimensions read consistently. A quick fix for drawings where text and dimension formatting has drifted.

name: MatchCrvDir
description: Flips the direction of curves to match a master curve. Worth running before lofting or sweeping, where mismatched curve directions cause twisted results.

name: MatchLayer
description: Moves selected objects onto the layer of a picked target object. Faster than hunting through the Layers panel when tidying a model's organisation.

name: MatchMapping
description: Copies texture mapping from a source object onto other objects so a material's pattern flows consistently across them. Saves redoing mapping widgets object by object.

name: MatchMeshEdge
description: Moves mesh vertices so neighbouring naked edges line up and close small gaps. Used when separate mesh parts almost meet but leave hairline cracks.

name: MatchProperties
description: Copies display and object properties such as layer, colour and linetype from one object to others. Fast way to bring rogue imports in line with your drawing standards.

name: MatchSrf
description: Adjusts a surface edge to meet a neighbouring surface with position, tangency or curvature continuity. The key tool for achieving seamless multi-patch surfaces in high-quality modelling.

name: Materials
description: Opens the Materials panel where render materials are created, edited and assigned. The main workspace for defining how surfaces look in renderings.

name: Maximize
description: Maximises the Rhino application window to fill the screen. A window-management convenience mainly used from scripts and macros.

name: MaxViewport
description: Toggles the active viewport between maximised and the multi-view layout. Usually driven by double-clicking the viewport title.

name: Merge2MeshFaces
description: Merges two adjacent mesh faces into a single face. A small-scale clean-up tool for simplifying unnecessarily triangulated areas of a mesh.

name: MergeAllCoplanarFaces
description: Dissolves unnecessary edges between flat faces that lie in the same plane. Tidies solids after booleans so they read cleanly and export with fewer faces.

name: MergeAllEdges
description: Merges adjacent edge segments along surface and polysurface borders into single edges wherever they meet smoothly. Tidies fragmented edge counts left behind by trims and joins.

name: MergeCoplanarFace
description: Merges a picked planar face of a polysurface with its adjacent coplanar faces, simplifying boxy solids after booleans. Reduces face clutter without changing the shape.

name: MergeEdge
description: Merges adjacent edge segments of a surface or polysurface into one edge. Use it on a specific edge chain when MergeAllEdges is more than you need.

name: MergeFaces
description: Combines adjacent SubD or mesh faces into a single larger face. Used to simplify topology after heavy editing.

name: MergeSrf
description: Combines two untrimmed surfaces sharing an edge into one single surface. Useful for simplifying models before offsetting, unrolling or exporting.

name: Mesh
description: Converts NURBS surfaces, polysurfaces or SubD into a polygon mesh with density controls. Used before 3D printing, export to game engines or heavy visualisation scenes.

name: MeshBooleanDifference
description: Subtracts one set of closed meshes from another. Used to cut openings in scan or export meshes without converting to NURBS.

name: MeshBooleanIntersection
description: Keeps only the shared volume of intersecting closed meshes. Handy for clash volumes and trimming context meshes to a site boundary.

name: MeshBooleanSplit
description: Splits meshes into parts along their mutual intersections, keeping all pieces. Useful for dividing terrain meshes along plot boundaries.

name: MeshBooleanUnion
description: Merges overlapping closed meshes into a single mesh. The mesh counterpart to BooleanUnion for print-ready models.

name: MeshBox
description: Creates a box directly as a mesh with set face counts. Useful for lightweight massing in mesh-based workflows and export pipelines.

name: MeshCone
description: Creates a cone as a polygon mesh. A quick faceted primitive for context and export models.

name: MeshCylinder
description: Creates a cylinder as a polygon mesh. Used where lightweight faceted geometry is preferable to NURBS, such as context models.

name: MeshEllipsoid
description: Creates an ellipsoid as a mesh primitive rather than a NURBS surface. Handy when building lightweight massing or export-ready mesh scenes.

name: MeshFromLines
description: Builds a mesh whose edges follow a network of intersecting lines. Useful for turning a drawn wireframe grid, such as a space-frame layout, directly into mesh faces.

name: MeshFromPoints
description: Creates mesh faces over an ordered grid of points. Useful for reconstructing terrain or scanned grids as a single mesh surface.

name: MeshIntersect
description: Intersects meshes with each other and returns the intersection as polylines. The mesh counterpart of Intersect, useful for section lines through scanned or exported models.

name: MeshOutline
description: Draws the outline of a mesh as seen from the current view as a planar curve. Great for site plan silhouettes of context models and quick shadow footprints.

name: MeshPatch
description: Fills a set of curves and points with a triangulated mesh patch. A quick route from surveyed contours or scattered spot levels to a terrain mesh.

name: MeshPlane
description: Creates a rectangular mesh plane with a set grid of faces. A common base for terrain sculpting and drape-style studies in mesh workflows.

name: MeshPolyline
description: Fills a closed polyline with mesh faces, turning an outline directly into a flat mesh. Useful for quick planar mesh panels without going through NURBS surfaces.

name: MeshRepair
description: Opens a guided panel that checks a mesh and walks through fixing its defects step by step. The first stop when a downloaded or scanned mesh refuses to print or boolean.

name: MeshSelfIntersect
description: Finds the places where a mesh passes through itself and marks them. An important check before 3D printing or exporting, where self-intersections cause failures.

name: MeshSphere
description: Creates a sphere as a polygon mesh with controllable density. Handy for placeholder objects in scenes destined for real-time or print output.

name: MeshSplit
description: Splits a mesh with curves, surfaces or other meshes without needing closed volumes. The general-purpose divider for open meshes like terrain.

name: MeshToNURB
description: Converts every mesh face into a NURBS surface joined as a polysurface. A blunt but effective route when downstream tools demand NURBS, best kept for small meshes.

name: MeshTorus
description: Creates a ring as a polygon mesh. Occasionally useful for faceted loops in visualisation scenes.

name: MeshTrim
description: Cuts away the picked side of a mesh along a curve or surface. Everyday tool for trimming site meshes to boundaries.

name: MeshTruncatedCone
description: Creates a truncated cone as a mesh primitive. One of the mesh equivalents of Rhino's solid primitives, for lightweight or export-focused modelling.

name: MigratePlugins
description: Brings plug-ins installed in a previous Rhino version across to the current one. Run it after upgrading so your toolset follows you.

name: Minimize
description: Minimises the Rhino application window to the taskbar. Mostly useful in scripts that hand control to another program temporarily.

name: Mirror
description: Reflects objects across a line or plane, optionally keeping the original. Essential for symmetrical plans, handed apartment types and reflected details.

name: MirrorHole
description: Mirrors an existing hole feature across a line on the same planar solid face. Quicker than cutting a matching hole from scratch on symmetrical parts.

name: ModelBasepoint
description: Sets the base point used when this file is inserted or linked into another model. Set it deliberately so blocks and references land where you expect, for example on a site datum.

name: ModifyRadius
description: Changes the radius of an existing circle or arc without redrawing it. A fast, precise edit for setting-out geometry.

name: Move
description: Moves objects from a base point to a target point with full snapping precision. The most fundamental transform, preferred over dragging when accuracy matters.

name: MoveEdge
description: Moves a single edge of a solid while the connected faces stretch to keep the body closed. Useful for tweaking wedge angles and ridge lines directly.

name: MoveFace
description: Pushes or pulls a face of a solid, extending the neighbouring faces to follow. Quick parametric-feeling edits like making a box taller or a recess deeper without remodelling.

name: MoveHole
description: Slides an existing hole to a new position within its planar face. Saves re-cutting openings when a penetration needs repositioning.

name: MoveTargetToObjects
description: Moves the view camera's target onto the selected objects so orbiting pivots around them. Cures the frustration of a view that rotates about empty space.

name: MoveUntrimmedEdge
description: Drags an untrimmed surface edge to a new position, reshaping the surface while keeping its structure. A direct-editing tool for simple surface adjustments.

name: MoveUVN
description: Nudges control points along a surface's U, V and normal directions with sliders and smoothing. A precise sculpting panel for refining surface interiors without breaking edges.

name: MPlane
description: Attaches a mobile construction plane to an object so the CPlane follows the object as it moves or rotates. Very useful when detailing components that sit at odd angles.

name: MultiPause
description: A macro helper that pauses a macro for any number of user picks until Enter is pressed. Use it where a plain Pause, which accepts one input, is not enough.

name: MultiPipe
description: Builds a smooth SubD pipe network over a set of connected curves, resolving the junctions automatically. Perfect for branching structures, node details and tubular furniture frames.

name: Named CPlanes
description: Opens the Named CPlanes panel, where construction planes can be saved and restored by name. Invaluable on projects with sloping or rotated setting-out grids.

name: Named Positions
description: Opens the Named Positions panel, which stores arrangements of objects so you can move things and later snap them back. Great for comparing design options or building exploded views.

name: Named Views
description: Opens the Named Views panel, where camera positions are saved and restored by name. The backbone of repeatable renders and consistent layout details.

name: NamedCPlane
description: Saves and restores construction planes by name. Keeps a library of working planes for each facade, roof pitch or datum in a project.

name: NamedPosition
description: Saves the current position of selected objects under a name so they can be returned there later, even after being moved. Useful for exploded axonometrics and option studies.

name: NamedSelections
description: Saves selection sets by name so a group of objects can be reselected in one click. A big time-saver for recurring edits on the same scattered set of geometry.

name: NamedView
description: Saves and restores camera positions by name, with thumbnails. Essential for repeatable render views and keeping agreed verified-view camera setups.

name: NetworkSrf
description: Builds a surface through a criss-crossing network of curves in two directions. Powerful for complex freeform patches where lofts and sweeps cannot capture the shape.

name: New
description: Starts a fresh model from a template that sets units and tolerances. Choosing the right template avoids tolerance headaches later.

name: NewFloatingViewport
description: Opens an extra viewport in its own window, ideal for a second monitor. Lets you keep a render view open while drafting in another.

name: NewViewport
description: Creates an additional viewport with its own camera and display settings. Useful for adding a dedicated perspective or detail view alongside the standard set.

name: NextDetail
description: Activates the next detail on the current layout. Lets you cycle through a sheet's views from the keyboard while setting them up.

name: NextOrthoViewport
description: Switches focus to the next orthographic viewport, cycling through plan and elevation views without reaching for the mouse. A small navigation convenience for multi-viewport work.

name: NextPerspectiveViewport
description: Switches focus to the next perspective viewport in the model. Useful when several perspective views are open for different camera studies.

name: NextU
description: Moves the control-point selection to the neighbouring point in the surface's U direction. Keyboard-friendly navigation for precise point editing on dense grids.

name: NextV
description: Moves the control-point selection to the neighbouring point in the surface's V direction. Pairs with NextU for stepping through a surface's point grid.

name: NextViewport
description: Makes the next viewport active, cycling through them in order. Quick keyboard navigation between views.

name: NextViewportToTop
description: Makes the next viewport active and brings it to the front. Useful when floating viewports overlap and the one you want is buried.

name: NoEcho
description: Stops commands echoing their text output to the command history. Used inside scripts and macros to keep the command line quiet while they run.

name: NonmanifoldMerge
description: Merges surfaces and polysurfaces into a single non-manifold polysurface, keeping shared internal faces rather than discarding them. Used in analysis and fabrication workflows where internal partitions matter.

name: Notes
description: Opens a simple text panel stored inside the model file. Useful for issue notes, modelling conventions and handover instructions that travel with the file.

name: Notifications
description: Opens the Notifications panel, which collects messages about updates, licensing and other events. Check it when the notification icon lights up.

name: Offset
description: Creates a parallel copy of a curve at a set distance, with corner and cap options. The backbone of wall thicknesses, clearance zones and repeated profile lines.

name: OffsetCrvOnSrf
description: Offsets a curve that lies on a surface so the copy stays on the surface at a true geodesic-style distance. Used for setting out seams and edge details on curved facades.

name: OffsetMesh
description: Offsets a mesh by a distance, optionally closing the result into a solid. The mesh equivalent of shelling, often used to give scanned or exported geometry a printable thickness.

name: OffsetMultiple
description: Offsets several curves at once by the same distance. Saves repeating Offset curve by curve when producing wall thicknesses or path edges across a drawing.

name: OffsetNormal
description: Offsets a curve that lies on a surface in the direction normal to that surface. Useful for building ribs, fins or upstands off doubly curved surfaces where a flat offset would be wrong.

name: OffsetSrf
description: Creates a copy of a surface or polysurface at a set distance along its normals, optionally building a closed solid between the two. The standard way to give architectural surfaces material thickness.

name: OffsetSubD
description: Offsets a SubD inwards or outwards, optionally building a closed solid shell between the two. The standard way to give sculpted skins a real material thickness.

name: OneLayerOff
description: Turns off the layer of an object you pick. A one-click declutter tool when you can see the offending geometry but do not know its layer name.

name: OneLayerOn
description: Turns on a single chosen layer and switches every other layer off. Instant focus when auditing one system, such as structure only.

name: OneView
description: Runs a single-viewport mode that swaps the construction plane automatically as you orbit near standard directions. A drafting-friendly way to work in one big view.

name: Open
description: Opens a Rhino model or any of the many supported CAD and mesh formats. Alongside Import, the gateway for consultant and manufacturer files.

name: Options
description: Opens Rhino's global settings for display, toolbars, aliases, modelling aids and more. Where you tune the environment to your own working style.

name: OptionsExport
description: Saves Rhino's options and settings out to a file. Use it to back up your setup or share office-standard settings across machines.

name: OptionsImport
description: Loads Rhino options and settings from a previously exported file. The other half of moving a familiar setup onto a new machine or standardising a team.

name: OptionsPage
description: Opens the Options dialog directly at a named page. Mainly used in toolbar buttons and macros that jump straight to a specific setting.

name: Orient
description: Moves, rotates and optionally scales objects by mapping two reference points onto two targets. A compound transform that places elements in one action instead of three.

name: Orient3Pt
description: Repositions objects by matching three reference points to three targets, fixing position and orientation in space. The reliable way to place a component onto a sloping plane.

name: OrientCameraToSrf
description: Aims the viewport camera perpendicular to a picked surface, looking straight at it. The quickest way to get a true face-on view of an angled facade or panel.

name: OrientCrvToEdge
description: Copies or moves a curve onto a surface edge, orienting it to match the edge. Handy for placing profile curves ready for sweeps along an edge.

name: OrientOnCrv
description: Places objects along a curve, orienting each to the curve direction. Useful for positioning individual elements like bollards where regular array spacing will not do.

name: OrientOnSrf
description: Places copies of an object onto a surface, aligned to the surface normal at each pick. Great for scattering rooflights or fixings across curved geometry by eye.

name: Ortho
description: Toggles constraint of cursor movement to set angle increments, typically 90 degrees. Fundamental drafting aid for keeping lines square.

name: OrthoAngle
description: Changes the angle that Ortho constrains to, which is 90 degrees by default. Set it to 30 or 45 degrees when working on angled grids or chamfered plans.

name: OrthoSnapToCPlaneZ
description: Toggles whether Ortho also constrains movement vertically along the construction plane's Z axis. Turn it on to draw and drag straight up and down while modelling in 3D.

name: Osnap
description: Opens the object snap controls for end, mid, centre, intersection and other precise picks. Accurate modelling in Rhino lives and dies by these snaps.

name: PackageManager
description: Browses, installs and updates plug-ins and resources from the official package server. The modern route to extending Rhino with tools like section utilities and renderers.

name: Pan
description: Slides the view across the model without changing zoom or angle. Basic navigation alongside Zoom and view rotation.

name: Parabola
description: Draws a parabola from focus or vertex definitions. Occasionally needed for reflector geometry, arch profiles and structural form studies.

name: Paraboloid
description: Draws a paraboloid surface, optionally capped into a solid. Useful for dish, reflector and canopy-style forms with true parabolic geometry.

name: Paste
description: Places clipboard contents into the model at their original coordinates. Completes the cut and copy clipboard workflow across files.

name: PasteAsBlock
description: Pastes the clipboard contents as a block instance rather than loose geometry. Useful for keeping repeated pasted elements lightweight and centrally editable.

name: PasteAt
description: Pastes the clipboard contents at a point you pick rather than at its original coordinates. Saves a paste-then-move step when bringing geometry between files.

name: Patch
description: Fits an approximate surface over a loose collection of curves, points or edges. A pragmatic hole-filler and terrain-builder when inputs are messy or incomplete.

name: Pause
description: A macro helper that pauses the macro for one user input, such as a pick or a value. The basic building block for interactive command macros.

name: PerspectiveAngle
description: Sets the lens angle of the perspective viewport's camera. Widen it for tight interior views, narrow it for flattering exterior shots with less distortion.

name: PerspectiveMatch
description: Matches the perspective camera to a background photograph by picking corresponding points, so the model lines up with the image. The key tool for dropping a proposal into a site photo.

name: Picture
description: Places an image in the model as a picture plane, commonly used to trace scanned drawings or display reference imagery. Successor to the old PictureFrame command.

name: Pipe
description: Wraps a solid circular section along any curve, with optional varying radii and caps. The fastest way to model handrails, service runs and structural tubes.

name: PlaceHole
description: Cuts a round hole into a planar face of a solid, with control over depth and direction. Faster and more deliberate than boolean-subtracting a cylinder by hand.

name: Plan
description: Sets the viewport to look straight down at the current construction plane. Instant return to true plan after working in 3D.

name: Planar
description: Toggles Planar mode, which keeps successive picks at the same construction-plane elevation as the previous point. Keeps 3D polylines and curves flat without constant elevator snapping.

name: PlanarDifference
description: Boolean-subtracts coplanar closed regions from one another, returning the trimmed 2D result. A drafting-style boolean for cleaning up overlapping outlines and hatch regions.

name: PlanarIntersection
description: Keeps only the overlapping area of coplanar closed regions, discarding the rest. Useful for finding the common footprint of stacked plan outlines.

name: PlanarMesh
description: Fills planar closed curves with a flat mesh, the mesh equivalent of PlanarSrf. Quick floors, panels and grounds for mesh-based scenes.

name: PlanarSrf
description: Creates flat surfaces from closed planar curves, including nested boundaries with holes. Everyday tool for turning plan outlines into floor plates and panels.

name: PlanarUnion
description: Merges coplanar closed regions into combined outlines, dissolving their overlaps. Good for consolidating overlapping plan shapes into a single boundary.

name: Plane
description: Draws a rectangular flat surface from corner to corner, with options for centre-out and three-point placement. The fastest way to make a ground plane, wall panel or backdrop.

name: PlaneThroughPt
description: Fits a rectangular plane through a set of points, averaging their positions. Useful for establishing a best-fit datum through surveyed or scanned data.

name: PlayAnimation
description: Plays back the animation set up with Rhino's animation tools, such as a turntable or sun study, in the viewport. Preview the motion before committing to recording frames.

name: PlugInManager
description: Lists installed plug-ins and lets you load, disable or install them. The place to go when a plug-in's commands stop appearing.

name: Point
description: Places a single point object at a picked or typed location. Useful for marking setting-out positions, snap targets and survey coordinates before drawing geometry.

name: PointCloud
description: Gathers selected point objects into a single point cloud, or breaks a cloud back into points. Keeps large scan or survey datasets manageable as one selectable object.

name: PointCloudSection
description: Cuts section profiles through a point cloud with a plane, extracting the points or polyline along the cut. The bridge from raw scan data to usable plan and section linework.

name: PointDeviation
description: Measures and colour-codes how far a set of points sits from a surface or mesh. Used to verify a rebuilt surface against original scan data.

name: PointGrid
description: Creates a rectangular grid of point objects. Useful as a scaffold for paving setouts, facade studies or anything needing a regular array of reference points.

name: Points
description: Places a run of point objects one after another until you press Enter. Quicker than repeating Point when plotting several markers or imported coordinate positions.

name: PointsOff
description: Hides control points when direct editing is finished. Prevents accidental dragging of points while working nearby.

name: PointsOn
description: Displays the control points of curves and surfaces so they can be dragged directly. The doorway into hands-on NURBS editing.

name: Polygon
description: Draws a regular polygon with any number of sides, inscribed or circumscribed about a radius. Handy for bolt patterns, kiosks and faceted plan forms.

name: PolygonCount
description: Reports how many render-mesh polygons the selection or scene contains. A quick weight check before exporting to real-time engines or worrying about display performance.

name: Polyline
description: Draws a connected chain of straight segments as one curve. Ideal for plan outlines, boundaries and any profile made of straight runs.

name: PolylineOnMesh
description: Draws a polyline whose points are constrained to a mesh surface. Ideal for sketching routes, paths or cut lines over scanned terrain.

name: PopupMenu
description: Opens the customisable pop-up command menu at the cursor, usually bound to the middle mouse button. Keeps favourite commands one click away without hunting through toolbars.

name: PopupPopular
description: Pops up a menu of your most-used commands at the cursor. A self-updating shortcut list based on how you actually work.

name: PopupToolbar
description: Pops up a chosen toolbar at the cursor for a quick pick, after which it disappears. Gives access to a whole toolbar without permanently docking it.

name: PrevDetail
description: Activates the previous detail on the current layout. Pairs with NextDetail for cycling through a sheet's views.

name: PrevU
description: Moves the control-point selection to the previous point in the surface's U direction. Part of the keyboard navigation set for precise point editing.

name: PrevV
description: Moves the control-point selection to the previous point in the surface's V direction. Part of the keyboard navigation set for precise point editing.

name: PrevViewport
description: Makes the previous viewport active, cycling backwards through them. The reverse of NextViewport.

name: Print
description: Sends layouts or viewports to a printer or PDF with scale, line width and colour controls. The final step in issuing drawings from Rhino.

name: PrintDisplay
description: Previews print output in the viewport, showing lineweights and print colours as they will plot. Check drawings with this on before sending anything to print.

name: Project
description: Projects curves or points straight down (or along a view direction) onto surfaces, polysurfaces or meshes. Used to push plan linework onto terrain or facade geometry.

name: ProjectToCPlane
description: Squashes objects flat onto the construction plane, optionally keeping the originals. Instantly turns 3D linework into a true 2D plan underlay.

name: Properties
description: Opens the panel showing the selected object's layer, colour, material and type-specific settings. The everyday place to check and adjust what something is.

name: PropertiesPage
description: Opens the Properties panel directly at a named page. Like OptionsPage, it exists mainly for toolbar buttons and macros that jump straight to a setting.

name: Pull
description: Pulls curves or points onto a surface by the shortest path rather than a fixed direction. Better than Project on steep or doubly curved surfaces where projection would distort placement.

name: Purge
description: Deletes unused layers, blocks, materials and other invisible data bloating the file. Often reclaims dramatic file size on long-running project models.

name: PushPull
description: Drags planar regions directly in or out to add or remove material, SketchUp-style. Introduced in Rhino 8, it makes fast massing edits without explicit boolean commands.

name: PushViewportToBack
description: Sends the active viewport behind the others in the stacking order. Useful for shuffling overlapping floating viewports.

name: Pyramid
description: Creates a solid pyramid with any number of base sides. Instant geometry for pyramidal roofs, skylights and obelisks.

name: QuadrangulateMesh
description: Merges pairs of triangles into quads where they lie close to planar. Tidies triangulated meshes into cleaner, lighter topology.

name: QuadRemesh
description: Rebuilds any mesh, surface or SubD as a clean quad-dominant mesh, optionally converting straight to SubD. Transforms scan data and faceted models into sculptable, well-flowing geometry.

name: Radiate
description: Applies live radial symmetry to a SubD so edits repeat around an axis. Added in Rhino 8 for rotationally patterned objects like lighting pieces and radial pavilions.

name: Radius
description: Reports the radius of a curve at a picked point. Quick verification that curved elements meet minimum bend or turning radii.

name: RailRevolve
description: Revolves a profile around an axis while its outer edge follows a rail curve, so the radius varies as it turns. Useful for shells and vault-like forms that are not purely circular in plan.

name: ReadCommandFile
description: Runs a plain text file of Rhino commands line by line. Simple batch automation without writing a proper script.

name: ReadEveryIGESEntity
description: An import troubleshooting toggle that forces Rhino to read every entity in an IGES file, including types normally skipped. Try it when an IGES import appears to be missing geometry.

name: ReadViewportsFromFile
description: Loads the viewport arrangement and views saved in another model file. Useful for standardising view setups across project files.

name: Rebuild
description: Reconstructs curves or surfaces with a chosen degree and control point count, evening out their structure. Standard clean-up before matching, deforming or exporting geometry.

name: RebuildCrvNonUniform
description: Refits a curve with non-uniformly spaced control points to a tolerance, placing fewer points on straight runs and more where the curve bends. Often gives cleaner results than plain Rebuild on mixed geometry.

name: RebuildEdges
description: Restores surface edges to their exact original positions after they have been forced by JoinEdge or drifted out of tolerance. A repair step when edge gaps start causing downstream failures.

name: RebuildMeshNormals
description: Recalculates a mesh's normals from its face geometry, discarding any custom vertex normals. The usual fix for odd shading on imported meshes.

name: RebuildUV
description: Rebuilds a surface in just the U or V direction with a chosen point count. Useful for evening out isocurve distribution in one direction while leaving the other intact.

name: RecordAnimation
description: Renders each frame of the set-up animation out to image files. The production step after previewing with PlayAnimation, ready for assembling into video.

name: Rectangle
description: Draws a rectangular polyline from two corners, a centre, or three points, with a rounded-corner option. The starting point for most plan footprints and panel outlines.

name: Redo
description: Reinstates the last change that Undo reversed. Handy when you step back one change too far.

name: RedoMultiple
description: Redoes several undone steps in one go. The counterpart to UndoMultiple for stepping back and forth through model history quickly.

name: RedoView
description: Re-applies a view change undone with UndoView. Lets you step forward again through camera history without re-navigating.

name: ReduceMesh
description: Lowers a mesh's polygon count while preserving its shape as far as possible. Essential for taming scan data and dense downloads before they slow the model.

name: ReducePolyline
description: Removes vertices from a polyline while keeping it within a tolerance of the original. Simplifies dense traced or imported polylines into manageable geometry.

name: RefitTrim
description: Refits a trimmed surface so a trimmed edge becomes a natural untrimmed edge. Valuable in continuity work, where matching and merging need untrimmed edges to succeed.

name: Reflect
description: Maintains a live mirrored half of a SubD so edits on one side update the other instantly. Invaluable for symmetrical furniture, vehicles and pavilion forms.

name: RefreshAllTextures
description: Reloads every texture image from disk, picking up edits made outside Rhino. Use it after tweaking a texture in an image editor so the viewport catches up.

name: RefreshShade
description: Discards and regenerates the display meshes of selected objects. The go-to fix when shaded surfaces look faceted, torn or out of date.

name: ReleaseFromCage
description: Disconnects objects from their cage-edit control object, freezing them in their current deformed shape. Do this once a cage deformation is final.

name: RemapCPlane
description: Re-orients objects from one construction plane to another, as if the geometry were drawn on the new plane. Excellent for moving 2D details onto sloped or vertical faces.

name: RememberCopyOptions
description: Toggles whether transform commands remember your last Copy yes/no choice between uses. Set it to suit whether you usually move or usually duplicate.

name: RemoveControlPoint
description: Deletes control points from a curve, or a whole row from a surface, letting the shape relax accordingly. Used to simplify over-defined geometry.

name: RemoveCrease
description: Returns creased SubD edges or vertices to smooth. Used when a hard edge should melt back into the surrounding form.

name: RemoveFromGroup
description: Takes selected objects out of their group while leaving the rest grouped. Useful for promoting one element out of a set for separate treatment.

name: RemoveGuide
description: Deletes guide lines placed with AddGuide. Keeps the infinite construction guides tidy once setting-out is done.

name: RemoveKnot
description: Deletes a knot from a curve or surface, simplifying its control structure with a slight shape change. Used to lighten over-detailed geometry before matching or exporting.

name: RemoveMappingChannel
description: Deletes a texture-mapping channel from the selected objects. Cleans up mapping setups that have accumulated unused channels.

name: RemoveMultiKnot
description: Removes stacked multiple knots from curves and surfaces, restoring smooth continuity where kinks were held. An advanced clean-up for geometry destined for high-quality surfacing.

name: RemovePerFaceColors
description: Strips per-face display colours from meshes and SubDs, returning them to their object colour. Undoes face-painting used during design studies.

name: RemoveSymmetry
description: Removes the symmetry constraint from a SubD so its mirrored halves can be edited independently. Use it once a symmetric form needs asymmetric refinement.

name: Render
description: Renders the current view with the active renderer into the render window. The starting point for presentation images beyond viewport captures.

name: RenderAssignMaterialToLayer
description: Assigns a render material to chosen layers so everything on them inherits it. The layer-based approach that keeps large models' materials manageable.

name: RenderAssignMaterialToLayersOfObjects
description: Assigns a render material to the layers that the selected objects sit on. A shortcut for layer-based materials when it is easier to pick objects than layer names.

name: RenderAssignMaterialToObjects
description: Assigns a render material directly to the selected objects, overriding their layer material. Use it for one-off material changes on individual elements.

name: RenderBlowup
description: Renders a picked region of the viewport enlarged, giving a high-resolution look at part of the frame. Useful for inspecting a detail without rendering the whole image at huge size.

name: Rendering
description: Opens the Rendering panel with the current renderer's settings, including resolution, quality and lighting options. Set things up here before pressing Render.

name: RenderInWindow
description: Renders only a rectangle of the view that you drag out. Saves time when you are iterating on one part of an image.

name: RenderMergeIdenticalMaterials
description: Merges duplicate identical render materials in the document into one. Declutters material lists bloated by imports and copy-pasting between files.

name: RenderOpenLastRendering
description: Reopens the most recent rendering saved with the file in the render window. Handy for revisiting the last result without re-rendering.

name: RenderOpenRenderImage
description: Opens a saved render image file in Rhino's render window, where post-effects and adjustments are available. Lets you revisit and tweak older renders.

name: RenderPreview
description: Renders the current view at draft quality for a fast check of composition, lighting and materials. Iterate here before committing to a full-quality render.

name: RenderPreviewInWindow
description: Renders a selected region of the view at draft quality. The quickest possible feedback loop when tuning one area of an image.

name: RenderPreviewWindow
description: Runs a draft-quality render in the render window. A quicker stand-in for Render while a scene is still evolving.

name: RenderReportImageFiles
description: Lists all the image and texture files the document references. Useful for auditing linked assets before archiving or sending a file to someone else.

name: RenderReportMissingImageFiles
description: Lists referenced texture and image files that cannot be found on disk. The first step in fixing renders full of missing-texture pink.

name: RenderWindow
description: Opens the render window showing the most recent render. Where render results live, along with save and post-effect options.

name: RepairSubD
description: Checks a SubD object for damaged or invalid structure and attempts to fix it. Reach for it when a SubD starts misbehaving after heavy editing or import.

name: Reparameterize
description: Changes the parameter domain of a curve or surface, for example to a 0-to-1 range, without altering its shape. Mostly matters for scripting, texture flow and flow-along-surface operations.

name: ReplaceBlock
description: Swaps selected block instances over to a different block definition. Perfect for replacing placeholder components, such as swapping massing trees for detailed ones.

name: Rescue3dmFile
description: Attempts to salvage geometry from a damaged or corrupt 3dm file. A last-resort recovery tool when a model will not open normally.

name: Reset
description: Restores Rhino's settings and window arrangement towards factory defaults. A troubleshooting reset for when the interface or behaviour has become unrecognisable.

name: ResetMessageBoxes
description: Re-enables warning dialogs previously dismissed with a do-not-show-again tick. Useful when a suppressed warning turns out to have mattered.

name: Restore
description: Restores the Rhino application window from a maximised or minimised state to its previous size and position. A window-management helper, mainly for scripts.

name: RevCloud
description: Draws a revision cloud around areas of change on a drawing. Added in Rhino 8 to support standard drawing issue and mark-up conventions.

name: Revert
description: Abandons unsaved changes and reloads the file from disk. The emergency exit after an experiment goes wrong beyond comfortable undoing.

name: Revolve
description: Spins a profile curve around an axis to create a surface of revolution. The fastest route to domes, columns, bowls and other rotationally symmetrical forms.

name: RevolvedHole
description: Cuts a hole with a revolved custom profile into a solid, ideal for countersinks, counterbores and chamfered recesses. More control than a plain round hole.

name: Rib
description: Adds a rib, a thin stiffening slab grown from a curve, onto a solid. A product-design feature tool that also suits fins and brackets in fabrication models.

name: Ribbon
description: Creates a ribbon: it offsets a curve and builds the surface between the curve and its offset. An instant flat strip for paths, borders and edging.

name: RibbonOffset
description: Offsets a curve while automatically resolving self-intersections, then builds a clean ribbon surface between curve and offset. Much more reliable than plain Offset around tight, complex outlines.

name: Rotate
description: Rotates objects around a centre point within the construction plane. Constant companion for orienting plans, furniture and site elements.

name: Rotate3D
description: Rotates objects around an axis you define by two points in space. Needed whenever the rotation is out of the construction plane, like tilting a roof panel.

name: RotateCamera
description: Swivels the camera in place, like turning your head rather than orbiting the model. Useful for interior views where the eye position must stay fixed.

name: RotateHole
description: Rotates an existing hole feature on a solid face to a new orientation without re-cutting it. Part of Rhino's hole-editing family alongside move and mirror.

name: RotateView
description: Orbits the camera around the view target. The keyboard-driven counterpart to right-mouse orbiting in perspective views.

name: RoundHole
description: Cuts a circular hole into a solid at a picked point, with depth and direction options. Faster than drawing a cylinder and boolean-subtracting for fixings and service penetrations.

name: Run
description: Launches an external program from within Rhino. Occasionally useful in scripted pipelines that hand files to other software.

name: RunPythonScript
description: Runs a Python script file, Rhino's main door to Python automation. The command behind most custom toolbar buttons that do clever things.

name: RunScript
description: Runs RhinoScript code or a script file. The classic automation route on Windows Rhino, predating the Python tools.

name: Save
description: Saves the current model, including its render meshes and previews. Frequent saving plus IncrementalSave is cheap insurance on live projects.

name: SaveACopy
description: Saves the current model to a new file while you carry on working in the original. Perfect for milestone snapshots and issuing versions without switching files.

name: SaveAs
description: Saves the model under a new name, location or earlier Rhino version. Also the route to handing files to consultants on older releases.

name: SaveAsTemplate
description: Saves the current file as a template, preserving its units, layers, annotation styles and settings for new projects. Build one good template and every project starts properly set up.

name: SaveRenderWindowAs
description: Saves the image in the render window to a file such as PNG or JPEG. The final step of getting a render out of Rhino and into a presentation.

name: SaveSmall
description: Saves without render meshes to produce a much smaller file. Standard practice before emailing or archiving large models.

name: SaveWindowLayout
description: Saves the current arrangement of panels and toolbars as a named window layout. Switch between task-specific setups, such as modelling versus drafting, in one step.

name: Scale
description: Resizes objects uniformly in all directions from an origin, by factor or reference distance. Used to correct imported drawing scales and resize elements proportionally.

name: Scale1D
description: Stretches objects along a single direction only. Ideal for lengthening a table, corridor or facade bay without changing its other proportions.

name: Scale2D
description: Scales objects in two directions while holding the third. Useful for resizing plans in plan-only without altering heights.

name: ScaleEach
description: Scales every selected object individually about its own base point, rather than the whole selection about one origin. Resize a field of repeated elements in place without them drifting apart.

name: ScaleNU
description: Scales objects by independent factors along X, Y and Z. The tool for squashing or stretching massing studies non-uniformly.

name: ScalePositions
description: Scales the distances between selected objects without resizing the objects themselves. Spread out or gather an arrangement, such as a furniture layout, while every piece keeps its size.

name: ScaleTextHeight
description: Scales the text height of selected annotations by a factor. The quick fix when notes and dimensions turn out the wrong size for the drawing scale.

name: ScreenCaptureToClipboard
description: Captures the active viewport, as displayed on screen, to the clipboard. The fastest route from model to email or slide deck.

name: ScreenCaptureToFile
description: Captures the active viewport, as displayed on screen, straight to an image file. Good for quick record shots without setting up a render.

name: ScriptEditor
description: Opens Rhino's script editor for writing, debugging and running Python and C# code. The modern home for automation, introduced alongside Rhino 8's scripting overhaul.

name: Section
description: Creates section curves where a picked plane slices through objects. Quick one-off cuts for studying profiles or extracting a single section line for drawings.

name: SectionStyles
description: Controls how clipped geometry displays at the cut, including hatch, fill and edge styling per object or layer. Part of the Rhino 8 sectioning workflow for drawing-quality live sections.

name: SelAll
description: Selects every visible, unlocked object in the model. Common first step before bulk transforms, exports or clean-ups.

name: SelAnnotationStyle
description: Selects all annotations that use a given annotation style. Ideal for auditing drawings or updating every note in one style at once.

name: SelBadObjects
description: Selects every invalid object in the model in one command. Pairs with Check to locate and repair or replace corrupt geometry.

name: SelBlockInstance
description: Selects block instances in the model. Useful before block-wide operations such as replacing or counting components.

name: SelBlockInstanceNamed
description: Selects every instance of a specific block definition by name. The quick way to grab all copies of one component, such as a particular window type.

name: SelBoundary
description: Selects objects using a closed boundary curve you pick as the selection region. Lets a drawn outline, such as a site boundary, do the selecting for you.

name: SelBrush
description: Selects objects by painting over them with a draggable brush. A natural fit for picking through cluttered areas where window selections grab too much.

name: SelBrushPoints
description: Selects control points by painting over them with a brush. Invaluable in sculpting workflows on dense point grids and SubD control cages.

name: SelCaptives
description: Selects every object currently captured by a control object, such as a cage created with CageEdit. Useful for checking which geometry is still being deformed by a cage before you edit or release it.

name: SelChain
description: Selects a run of curves or edges connected end to end from one pick. Speeds up choosing rails and boundaries for sweeps, lofts and fillets.

name: SelChildren
description: Adds the history children of the current selection - the objects that were built from it and update when it changes. Reach for it when you need everything that depends on a parent curve or surface.

name: SelCircular
description: Selects objects by dragging a circular region in the viewport rather than the usual rectangular window, with window or crossing behaviour. Handy for grabbing everything around a point, such as a column and its fittings.

name: SelClippingPlane
description: Selects all clipping plane objects in the model. Clipping planes are often hard to pick amongst dense geometry, so this gathers them in one go for moving, hiding or deleting.

name: SelClippingPlaneInViewport
description: Selects only the clipping planes that affect the active viewport. Useful in models where different views carry different section cuts and you want to adjust just the ones cutting the current view.

name: SelClosedCrv
description: Selects all closed curves in the model in one go. Handy when preparing profiles for extrusion or checking which outlines are ready to become surfaces.

name: SelClosedMesh
description: Selects all closed, watertight meshes - the ones ready for 3D printing or Boolean work. A quick audit before export.

name: SelClosedPolysrf
description: Selects every closed polysurface - that is, watertight solids. Useful for auditing a model before Boolean operations, sectioning or volume calculations.

name: SelClosedSrf
description: Selects all closed single surfaces, such as spheres and tori. Pairs with SelOpenSrf when sorting a model by what is sealed and what is not.

name: SelClosedSubD
description: Selects all closed SubD objects - those with no open edges. Handy when checking which SubD forms are watertight before converting or printing.

name: SelColor
description: Selects all objects displaying a chosen colour. Useful for rounding up imports whose colours came in by object rather than layer.

name: SelConnected
description: Grows a sub-object selection on a mesh or SubD to include everything topologically connected to it. Saves laborious clicking when you need a whole region of faces or edges.

name: SelConnectedMeshFaces
description: From a picked face, selects all the mesh faces joined to it. Useful for grabbing one shell of a mesh that actually contains several disjoint pieces.

name: SelControls
description: Selects the control objects, such as CageEdit cages, that are deforming other geometry. Pairs with SelCaptives when tidying up or removing cage-editing set-ups.

name: SelCrossing
description: Runs a crossing selection: drag a window and anything the rectangle touches is selected, not only what sits fully inside. The explicit command form is mainly useful in macros and scripts.

name: SelCrv
description: Selects all curve objects in one hit. Ideal for bulk operations like moving construction linework to its own layer.

name: SelDetail
description: Selects detail viewports on the active layout. Handy when a detail's border is hard to pick, or you want every detail at once before locking them against accidental panning.

name: SelDim
description: Selects every dimension in the model. A quick way to gather annotation for moving to a dedicated layer, restyling or purging.

name: SelDimAngular
description: Selects all angular dimensions, leaving other annotation alone. Useful when a drawing's angle callouts need restyling or checking as a set.

name: SelDimCentermark
description: Selects all centre-mark annotations - the cross marks placed at circle and arc centres - so they can be restyled or tidied as a set.

name: SelDimLinear
description: Selects all linear and aligned dimensions in one go, so a drawing's main measurements can be restyled or moved together.

name: SelDimOrdinate
description: Selects all ordinate dimensions - the datum-based callouts used on fabrication drawings - so they can be managed as a set.

name: SelDimOverride
description: Selects dimensions whose annotation-style settings have been overridden on the object. Useful for auditing drawings where individual dimensions have drifted from the document standard.

name: SelDimRadial
description: Selects all radius and diameter dimensions, handy when circular callouts need checking or restyling across a drawing.

name: SelDimTextOverride
description: Selects dimensions whose displayed text has been typed over rather than showing the true measured value. Well worth running before issuing drawings, so faked figures do not slip through.

name: SelDot
description: Selects all annotation dots - the screen-facing labels that keep a constant size. Useful for restyling or clearing markers scattered through a model.

name: SelDup
description: Selects objects that are exact duplicates sitting on top of others. The classic pre-delete step for cleaning files bloated by double geometry.

name: SelDupAll
description: Selects all duplicate objects including the originals, unlike SelDup which leaves one copy of each unselected. Use it to review a duplication problem before deciding what to keep.

name: Select
description: Command-line object selection: prompts you to pick objects and adds them to the current selection. Mostly used inside macros and scripts where an explicit selection step is needed.

name: SelectionFilter
description: Opens the selection filter control, which limits picking to chosen object types such as curves, surfaces or annotation. Invaluable in dense models where clicks keep landing on the wrong thing.

name: SelectionFilterEdges
description: Sets the selection filter so that picks grab edge sub-objects of surfaces, meshes and SubDs without holding Ctrl+Shift. Turn it off again once the edge work is done.

name: SelectionFilterEnable
description: Switches the selection filter on or off without changing its settings - a quick escape when the filter is blocking normal picking.

name: SelectionFilterFaces
description: Sets the selection filter so that picks grab face sub-objects, useful for repeated face-level editing on SubDs, meshes and polysurfaces.

name: SelectionFilterNone
description: Clears every tick in the selection filter so nothing can be picked - mainly used at the start of macros before enabling only the types wanted.

name: SelectionFilterToggle
description: Toggles the selection filter between enabled and disabled while keeping its current settings, so you can flip in and out of filtered picking quickly.

name: SelectionFilterVertices
description: Sets the selection filter so that picks grab vertex and control-point sub-objects - useful for stretches of point-level editing on meshes and SubDs.

name: SelEdgeLoop
description: From one picked edge, selects the whole edge loop running across a mesh or SubD. Essential in SubD modelling for creasing, deleting or transforming a complete feature line at once.

name: SelEdgeRing
description: Selects an edge ring - the parallel edges marching around a mesh or SubD - from a single pick. Complements SelEdgeLoop when harvesting topology for editing.

name: SelExtrusion
description: Selects all lightweight extrusion objects in the model. Useful when you need to convert them to polysurfaces for editing, or to see what UseExtrusions has been creating.

name: SelFaceLoop
description: Selects a run of faces forming a loop across a SubD or mesh from one picked face - quick material for extruding, colouring or deleting a whole strip.

name: SelFacesToBoundary
description: Grows a face selection on a SubD or mesh outwards until it reaches a boundary such as creases, open edges or selected edges - a fast way to fill a bounded region of faces.

name: SelFence
description: Selects by drawing a freehand fence line through the model; anything the line crosses is selected. Good for picking a scattered string of objects in one stroke.

name: SelFontUse
description: Selects the text and annotation that use a particular font. Useful when standardising drawings, or hunting down notes set in the wrong typeface after a file swap.

name: SelGroup
description: Selects a group by choosing its name from a list - a lifesaver when groups are buried in a crowded model or sit off screen.

name: SelHatch
description: Selects every hatch in the model, useful for moving all fills to their own layer or adjusting them after a drawing revision.

name: SelHatchPattern
description: Selects all hatches that use a specified pattern - for example, to swap every brick hatch for a different style in one edit.

name: SelID
description: Selects an object by typing or pasting its unique identifier (GUID). Mostly a scripting and troubleshooting tool - for instance, chasing down an object reported by an audit command.

name: SelLast
description: Reselects the objects changed or created by the most recent command. Invaluable for chaining operations, like moving what you just imported.

name: SelLayer
description: Selects every object on layers you choose. Combines with hide, export or transform commands for layer-wide operations.

name: SelLayerNumber
description: Selects everything on a layer identified by its position number in the layer list. Largely a legacy and scripting convenience - most people select by layer name instead.

name: SelLeader
description: Selects all leaders - the arrowed annotation callouts - so they can be restyled, re-layered or purged together.

name: SelLight
description: Selects all light objects - spotlights, point lights, rectangular lights and the rest - which are often awkward to click in a busy scene.

name: SelLine
description: Selects all straight line curves, ignoring arcs and freeform curves. Handy when cleaning up imported CAD linework or isolating construction lines.

name: SelLinetype
description: Selects objects drawn with a given linetype - useful when reorganising imported drawings where dashed, chain and continuous lines carry different meanings.

name: SelMappingWidget
description: Selects texture-mapping widgets - the box, sphere or plane gizmos that control how textures wrap objects - so you can move or scale them. They are easy to lose track of in the viewport.

name: SelMaterialName
description: Selects every object that uses a particular material, chosen by name. A quick way to audit or re-assign materials across a scene before rendering.

name: SelMesh
description: Selects all mesh objects. Convenient for isolating imported context meshes from native NURBS work.

name: SelMeshEdges
description: Selects mesh edge sub-objects, gathering edges so operations such as extraction, welding or creasing can act on them directly.

name: SelMeshFacesByArea
description: Selects mesh faces whose area falls within a range you set. Great for finding sliver faces in scan data or exports before repairing or deleting them.

name: SelMeshFacesByAspectRatio
description: Selects mesh faces by their aspect ratio, flagging the long thin faces that cause shading artefacts and analysis problems. A useful triage step on meshes destined for rendering or simulation.

name: SelMeshFacesByDraftAngle
description: Selects mesh faces whose draft angle relative to a pull direction falls within a set range. Useful when checking mouldability, CNC tool access or overhangs for 3D printing on mesh models.

name: SelMeshFacesByEdgeLength
description: Selects mesh faces with edges longer or shorter than limits you set, helping to locate over-coarse patches or degenerate slivers in a mesh.

name: SelMeshPart
description: Selects one connected piece of a mesh that contains several disjoint parts - pick a face and the whole part highlights, ready to split off or delete. Common when dissecting scan meshes.

name: SelMirroredBlocks
description: Selects block instances that have been mirrored (negatively scaled). Worth running before export or fabrication, as mirrored blocks can misbehave in other applications.

name: SelNakedMeshEdgePt
description: Selects the mesh vertices lying on naked, unjoined edges, showing exactly where a mesh fails to close. Follow up with welding or edge-matching tools to shut the gaps before printing.

name: SelName
description: Selects objects by their assigned object name. Depends on disciplined naming, but then gives instant pinpoint selection in large files.

name: SelNamedViewWidget
description: Selects named-view widgets - the camera markers displayed in the model for saved views - so they can be moved, hidden or deleted.

name: SelNone
description: Clears the current selection entirely. Useful in scripts and when Escape is mapped elsewhere.

name: SelNonManifold
description: Selects non-manifold edges, where more than two faces meet along one edge - a defect that breaks 3D printing and Boolean operations. Use it alongside ZoomNonManifold to inspect each problem spot.

name: SelObjectsWithHistory
description: Selects every object carrying construction history, so you can see what will update when parent geometry changes - or purge history before sending a file out.

name: SelOpenCrv
description: Selects all open curves - the ones that fail to close into loops. The usual first step when hunting gaps in linework destined for extrusion or planar surfaces.

name: SelOpenMesh
description: Selects all meshes with naked edges - the ones not yet watertight. A quick audit before 3D printing or Boolean work.

name: SelOpenPolysrf
description: Selects every open polysurface - joined surfaces that do not seal into a solid. Run it before Booleans or volume calculations to find the leaky models.

name: SelOpenSrf
description: Selects all open single surfaces, complementing SelClosedSrf when sorting a model by what is sealed and what is not.

name: SelOpenSubD
description: Selects all SubD objects with open edges - the unfinished or deliberately open forms - so they can be reviewed or closed up.

name: SelParents
description: Adds the history parents of the current selection - the input geometry that drives it. Useful for finding which curve to edit when you want a lofted or extruded surface to update.

name: SelPicture
description: Selects all picture objects - reference images placed with the Picture command - which tend to hide behind geometry and resist picking.

name: SelPlanarCrv
description: Selects all curves that lie flat in a plane - the ones eligible for PlanarSrf, hatching or clean extrusion. Anything left unselected probably has a stray point off-plane.

name: SelPlanarSrf
description: Selects all planar surfaces - flat faces such as floor plates and panels - which is useful before flattening, hatching or replacing them with simpler geometry.

name: SelPolyline
description: Selects all polylines - curves made purely of straight segments - handy for isolating imported CAD linework or set-out geometry from freeform curves.

name: SelPolysrf
description: Selects all polysurfaces, including closed solids. Quick filter when exporting or re-layering built massing.

name: SelPrev
description: Restores the previous selection set. A lifesaver after accidentally deselecting a painstaking multi-pick.

name: SelPt
description: Selects every point object. Typical use is deleting leftover setting-out or divide points before issuing a model.

name: SelPtCloud
description: Selects all point cloud objects, which are otherwise fiddly to pick amongst geometry. Useful when managing survey and scan data alongside a model.

name: SelRectangular
description: Rectangular region selection as an explicit command, with window and crossing options - chiefly useful inside macros where the selection method must be spelt out.

name: SelRenderColor
description: Selects objects whose render colour matches one you specify - a way of grouping geometry by colour in models where materials were assigned loosely.

name: SelSelfIntersectingCrv
description: Selects curves that cross themselves. Self-intersections wreck offsets, extrusions and planar surfaces, so this is a key clean-up check on imported or traced linework.

name: SelShortCrv
description: Selects curves shorter than a length you give - the classic way to find the stray slivers left behind by exploding, importing or aggressive trimming.

name: SelSmall
description: Selects objects smaller than a size you give. Excellent for catching slivers and debris left over from trims and imports.

name: SelSrf
description: Selects every single-surface object in the model. Useful for separating unjoined surfaces from finished polysurfaces during clean-ups.

name: SelSubD
description: Selects all SubD objects in the model. Useful when converting or re-layering sculpted concept geometry en masse.

name: SelSubDEdges
description: Selects SubD edge sub-objects, gathering edges ready for creasing, bevelling or transforming without picking them one by one.

name: SelSubDFriendlyCrv
description: Selects curves that are SubD-friendly - degree 3 with uniform structure - and therefore behave well as inputs to SubD tools. Anything unselected may need MakeSubDFriendly first.

name: SelText
description: Selects all text objects in the model, useful for restyling notes, moving them to an annotation layer or checking fonts across a drawing set.

name: SelTrimmedSrf
description: Selects all trimmed surfaces - those whose underlying surface has been cut back by trims. Useful before shrinking, untrimming or checking a model for export.

name: SelU
description: With control points on, selects an entire row of points running in the surface's U direction from a single pick - far faster than window-selecting rows when sculpting surfaces.

name: SelUntrimmedSrf
description: Selects all untrimmed surfaces - full four-sided sheets with no cuts - complementing SelTrimmedSrf when auditing how a model was built.

name: SelUV
description: Selects the crossing rows of control points in both the U and V directions through a picked point, giving a cross-shaped selection for symmetrical surface editing.

name: SelV
description: With control points on, selects an entire row of points running in the surface's V direction from a single pick - the partner to SelU for fast row-based surface editing.

name: SelVisible
description: Selects only the objects actually visible in the current viewport, ignoring geometry hidden behind other objects in shaded views. Good for grabbing exactly what a client sees in a particular view.

name: SelVolumeObject
description: Selects objects inside or crossing a closed solid you pick - selection by real 3D volume rather than a screen window. Useful for harvesting everything within a massing volume or zone.

name: SelVolumePipe
description: Selects objects inside an imaginary pipe along a curve - for example, everything within a set distance of a route, cable run or road centreline.

name: SelVolumeSphere
description: Selects objects inside a sphere you define by centre and radius - a true three-dimensional radius search around a point in the model.

name: SelWindow
description: Window selection as an explicit command: only objects entirely inside the dragged rectangle are selected. Mainly for macros and scripts that need the method spelt out.

name: SendBackward
description: Moves the selected object one step back in the draw order, changing how overlapping curves, hatches and pictures stack on screen and in prints. Draw order matters most in 2D drawing and presentation work.

name: SendToBack
description: Sends the selected object to the very back of the draw order, so everything else displays and prints on top of it - the usual treatment for background images and fills.

name: SetActiveViewport
description: Makes a named viewport the active one from the command line - a scripting and macro building block rather than something you would type by hand.

name: SetCurrentRenderPlugIn
description: Chooses which installed render engine - Rhino Render or a third-party renderer - the Render command and render tools drive. Switch here when a project moves between quick previews and production rendering.

name: SetDimensionLayer
description: Nominates a layer that new dimensions and annotation land on automatically, keeping drawing notes off your modelling layers without constant layer switching.

name: SetDisplayMode
description: Switches the viewport between display modes such as Wireframe, Shaded, Rendered, Ghosted, Arctic and Raytraced. Different modes suit drafting, design review and presentation checking.

name: SetDocumentUserText
description: Attaches key-value text data to the document itself - job numbers, revision notes, project metadata - which scripts, Grasshopper and title-block fields can read back.

name: SetFlythroughAnimation
description: Sets up a fly-through animation in which the camera travels along a path curve you choose, and Rhino records the frames. The classic way to walk a client through a scheme.

name: SetGroupName
description: Renames an existing group so it can be found and selected by a meaningful name later - worth doing as models grow and 'Group01' stops meaning anything.

name: SetIgesLayerLevelMap
description: Controls how Rhino layers map to level numbers when exchanging IGES files - needed when a receiving CAD system expects a particular level convention.

name: SetLayerLinetype
description: Assigns a linetype to a layer from the command line, so everything on that layer inherits it - the scriptable counterpart to setting it in the Layers panel.

name: SetLayerToObject
description: Makes the current layer whichever layer a picked object sits on - a very quick way to start drawing on the same layer as existing work without opening the Layers panel.

name: SetLinetype
description: Applies a linetype to the selected objects, overriding what their layer would give them - dashed for demolition, chain for centrelines and so on.

name: SetLinetypeScale
description: Sets the global scale factor applied to linetype patterns, so dashes and chains read correctly at your model units and print scales.

name: SetMaximizedViewport
description: Maximises a named viewport so it fills the graphics area - mainly used in scripts and toolbar macros to jump straight to a particular working view.

name: SetObjectDisplayMode
description: Overrides the display mode of selected objects in a viewport - for instance keeping context buildings wireframe while your proposal shows rendered. One of the best tricks for readable working views and illustrative screenshots.

name: SetObjectName
description: Gives the selected object a name, visible in Properties and usable by selection and reporting tools - the foundation of tidy, searchable models.

name: SetOneDaySunAnimation
description: Creates a sun-study animation across a single day: Rhino steps the sun through its positions for a chosen date and location and records the frames. Ideal for shadow studies supporting planning applications.

name: SetOrtho
description: Turns ortho mode on or off from the command line, constraining cursor movement to set angles - the scriptable twin of the status bar's Ortho pane.

name: SetPathAnimation
description: Animates the camera along a path curve while it aims at a target you define, then records the frames - more controllable than a freehand fly-through for rehearsed presentation routes.

name: SetPerFaceColorByFacePack
description: Colours each face pack of a SubD with its own flat colour, making visible how faces will group together when the object converts to NURBS. A diagnostic aid for judging SubD topology.

name: SetPlanar
description: Toggles planar mode, which keeps successively picked points at the same construction-plane elevation - helpful when tracing plans or drawing flat linework in a 3D view.

name: SetPt
description: Flattens selected objects or control points to a shared X, Y or Z value. The classic tool for levelling points onto a datum, such as zeroing survey linework to Z0.

name: SetRedrawOff
description: Suspends viewport redrawing so scripts and macros run without screen flicker and repaint slowdowns. Pair it with SetRedrawOn when the script finishes.

name: SetRedrawOn
description: Restores viewport redrawing after SetRedrawOff, refreshing the screen so you can see the results of a script's work.

name: SetSeasonalSunAnimation
description: Creates a sun study across the year, animating the sun's position at a fixed time of day through the seasons - useful for solstice-to-solstice shadow and daylight comparisons.

name: SetSnap
description: Sets the grid snap spacing and toggles grid snap from the command line - useful in scripts and when setting up drafting-style precision for orthogonal work.

name: SetSpotlightToView
description: Moves the selected spotlight so it shines from the current viewport's camera position: aim the view where you want light, run the command, and the light matches it.

name: SetTurntableAnimation
description: Sets up a turntable animation in which the camera orbits around the model (or the model appears to spin), recording the frames. The standard product-shot style presentation of an object or massing model.

name: SetUserText
description: Attaches key-value text data to selected objects - door numbers, finishes, cost codes - which the Properties panel, scripts and Grasshopper can read back. The lightweight route to data-rich models.

name: SetView
description: Points the viewport at a standard direction such as Top, Front, Right or Perspective, in world or CPlane terms. The command behind the standard view buttons.

name: SetViewFocusDistance
description: Sets the camera's focus distance for the active view, which depth-of-field effects in raytraced display and rendering use to decide what appears sharp.

name: SetViewToSpotlight
description: Points the active viewport's camera to match a spotlight, so you see exactly what the light covers - invaluable when aiming accent lighting in interiors.

name: SetWorkingFolder
